{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1o5dt2 (SUNID 103884; 1o5d T:107–205) has the domain-specific flag fr: “fragment; missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence.” d1uc6a1 (SUNID 107766; 1uc6 A:6–109) has no corresponding inconsistency annotation. Similar residue-number spans therefore do not establish equivalent completeness.

For alignment, align the reliably corresponding, observed domain core using sequence and structural evidence; mask unavailable regions as missing data rather than interpreting them as evolutionary deletions. Report aligned length and coverage alongside identity or structural similarity: a good match over the fragment does not demonstrate full-domain agreement. Check deposited coordinates, sequence coverage, and construct boundaries to establish exactly what is absent; the flag alone does not identify the missing elements or their cause.

For a general family representative or full-domain template, prefer d1uc6a1 over the flagged fragment if its completeness and structural quality are verified. Absence of a fragment flag is not itself proof of completeness or optimal quality. Retain d1o5dt2 as a supplementary representative of tissue factor or as a template for its covered region, explicitly marking its limitations; do not use it alone to reconstruct missing regions or define the complete family architecture.

Both remain members of Fibronectin type III family b.1.2.1 (SUNID 49266), supporting family-level homology. Their superfamily is b.1.2 (49265); the broader immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich fold b.1 (48725) and all-beta class b (48724) do not alone establish common ancestry. d1uc6a1 is from human ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 is from human tissue factor. These different protein contexts illustrate family diversity, but truncation must not be counted as a novel fold, genuine domain shortening, or unusually strong divergence without independent evidence. Neither family membership nor the fragment annotation justifies transferring their specific receptor, ligand-binding, or coagulation functions. Diversity analyses should retain the fragment annotation, compare equivalent covered regions, and check conclusions against complete, nonredundant domains.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1uc6a1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1o5dt2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/b.1.2.1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/107766","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103884","/api/v1/openapi.yaml","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations"]}]}
